guardContracts.conclusion: oZ is a capability gate, not a direct work/codex product-mode test. allowWork=true selects chatgpt.conversations; that access policy accepts either chatgpt product access or an allowed workCloud policy. The in_app_chat configFeature is still part of the capability contract.
conditions: allowWork defaults false. false selects chatgpt, waits for both product and chatgpt.seat-access loading, and shows lazy ChatSeatAccessScreen when seat-access is capable.
true selects chatgpt.conversations and skips the seat-access loading/screen branches. Missing selected capability redirects /.
Both modes wrap allowed children in Suspense. Capability evaluator combines policy, statsig, settings and configFeature results; it is not a filename classifier.
unknowns: Effective app-server in_app_chat feature values, current Statsig flags, account/workspace policies and downstream page checks remain unobserved.
This does not establish that every chatgpt-named page is required by the requested standalone Codex scope.

guardContracts.conclusion: The actual Route alias vh mounts ChatGptConversationPage at /c/:conversationId and /g/:gizmoId/c/:conversationId through oZ(allowWork=true) and WKa. Static routing therefore does not make these pages exclusive to a chat sidebar mode.
conditions: UFs lazily imports ChatGptConversationPage. Both actual route elements set allowWork:true.
Path aliases trace eVe -> shared export mMt -> LDn=/c/:conversationId; MFe -> hMt -> RDn=/g/:gizmoId/c/:conversationId.
unknowns: Downstream ChatGptConversationPage internals were not parsed in this narrow review; final runtime availability and whether retained Work/cloud task flows need this page remain unknown.

conditions: WEB: prefix redirects /.

guardContracts.conclusion: ChatGptProjectSettingsDialog is a shared-project candidate: the same pss sidebar function contains a sidebarProductMode===work branch, a local Codex task action, linked local-project handling, and the settings-dialog call. Its settings call is not conditioned on sidebarProductMode===chat.
conditions: pss reads R=Zs(gPt,previewNavigationState?.sidebarProductMode), computes V=R===work && flag, and H=V && no linkedLocalProject.
The same function labels an action as starting a local Codex task in a ChatGPT project and invokes FSi via the work/local action.
Settings open sets ae true; final dialog condition is ae && Omn(project). Omn only checks isCachedSidebarProject!==true.

unknowns: Upstream sidebar visibility, final platform guard, project data, account entitlement, linked-project feature flags and downstream dialog rules remain unverified.
The proof supports avoiding name-based deletion; it does not claim the dialog is reachable in every Codex-only profile.

guardContracts.conclusion: The sidebar product resolver is access/config-dependent and produces chat/work from its explicit branches and persistedMode. This resolver alone cannot classify entire chunks as Codex-only or ChatGPT-only.
conditions: gPt supplies chatgpt access, seat access, persistedMode, Work loading/availability and work-only flag to lPt.
lPt returns work for extension or workOnlyModeEnabled, otherwise chooses persistedMode/chat/work/undefined based on capability and Work inputs.
The separate primary project-display branch uses work/codex labels, showing that these strings belong to different contexts and should not be merged into one unverified mode taxonomy.
unknowns: Effective flags and persisted mode were not observed; global app product mapping remains unknown.

guardContracts.conclusion: sFs is the dedicated project-entry wrapper. Its final content branch uses oZ with default allowWork=false, but it can redirect to / with chatGptProjectId state before reaching that wrapper. This dedicated entry condition does not make shared project/settings components or local Codex project tasks equivalent to the ChatGPT chat mode or automatically excludable.
conditions: The actual vh registration at /g/:projectId/project has element sFs. sFs extracts the project identifier from pathname and reads LOCAL_PROJECTS, auth readiness, account-scoped local-project mappings, flag 2880010779, and gate 2929091547.
If no project ID exists, it returns null. With gate 2929091547 false and the linked-project flag enabled, it waits when auth is not ready or account scope exists but LOCAL_PROJECTS data is absent.

bu resolves to y7r; y7r uses x7r to find a local project paired through chatGptBacking with matching accountId/userId. x7r excludes IDs starting g-p- and accepts only a unique pairing for each ChatGPT project. It reads static project structures here; no real values were inspected.

With gate 2929091547 false and no mapped local project, sFs returns null while its same-gate signal s is true; otherwise it Navigate-replaces / with state {chatGptProjectId:projectId}. Gate true bypasses these mapping wait/redirect branches.
The final branch renders oZ({children:OJa({routeProjectId})}); allowWork is absent, therefore the existing oZ default chatgpt/seat-access capability branches apply.

Existing pss evidence contains sidebarProductMode===work, local Codex task creation, linked local projects and an independent settings-dialog call. Its project-open action also uses gate 2929091547 and preserves chatGptProjectId in a home navigation fallback. These cross-references are different from the dedicated sFs final-content gate.
unknowns: The effective flags, auth status, actual account-scoped mappings, s signal value, parent route guards and OJa downstream rules remain unverified.
The observed branch to home preserves project context; this static review does not establish which runtime composer mode consumes it.

Whether the reconstruction should keep, adapt, or remove this particular project-entry URL requires a retained-feature decision. It cannot justify deleting shared settings or Codex task/project contracts by component name.

projectReviewReferences.conclusion: The entire 98-byte module imports app-initial.akn as e and okn as t, invokes t, and re-exports e as fetchChatGptProject. There is no local request implementation or product-mode guard. The re-exported implementation must be classified using existing upstream contracts/callers.

The exported Pt component binds project save to app-initial.iOn, source upload hook to oOn, deletion hook to sOn, local-folder eligibility to fkn and edit capability to gkn. The same dialog conditionally renders local-folders-section.t under s && L && je(i). Its direct safeGet requests for gizmo details and connector scopes are separate from those imported mutation implementations. A module-name based removal would discard the explicit local-folder branch; upstream local/remote mutation contracts and caller guards are required.

Pt binds t to app-shared.$wt and issues safeGet for /gizmos/{gizmo_id_or_short_url} and /projects/{project_id}/connector_scopes. The details query is enabled only on advanced view when instructions or memory_scope is missing. Connector loading is enabled by Lt(project), whose complete function tests gizmo_snorlax_type == null. These predicates are data/view conditions, not independently proven Work/ChatGPT product-mode gates. The existing TFt/AW wrapper contract does not directly bind the different imported $wt facade.

The entire module exports a project_save metadata parser (t/o), timestamp normalizer (n/s), initializer (r/f) and source-type message descriptor table (i/d). It contains no direct network/IPC/project mutation. The settings module imports all four exports for its source rows. Project-save field names and message labels do not establish whether local project support may be removed.

projectReviewReferences.conclusion: Existing full pss/Dos/jos evidence traces the same lazy ChatGptProjectSettingsDialog export into shared sidebar project/settings use. pss includes Work and local Codex task context; its dialog condition is ae && Omn(project), without a ChatGPT-only sidebar mode condition. In contrast, dedicated sFs project-route finally uses oZ without allowWork, hence the documented default false guard. Its earlier mapping redirects can pass chatGptProjectId through state. That route cannot be treated as the exclusive caller or exclusion boundary for shared project settings/local task handling.
